requirement:
`languages::PlainText` implements `OutlineLang` under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider`. Its default value is
cheaply cloneable and claims no extensions. The filename-based constructors
select it when no supplied language claims the extension, including filenames
without an extension, under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults`.
rationale:
structural: The structural obligations in `requirements.sdk.sources.plain-text.language` are these. `languages::PlainText` implements `OutlineLang`. Its default value is cheaply cloneable. It claims no extensions.

- **Implements `OutlineLang`.** The invocation `language!(PlainText, super::plain::PROFILE)` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/languages/mod.rs` (root `macro@8f870aac097a`) expands the `macro[language]` macro. That macro declares `pub struct PlainText` and `impl super::OutlineLang for PlainText`. The impl has `name`, `extensions`, `outline`, `fingerprint_scheme` and `search_structure`. An alternative that only exposed free functions, with no trait impl, would break the clause "implements `OutlineLang`". So this clause is structural, and the root covers it.
- **Default value, cheaply cloneable.** The macro puts `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]` on a unit struct. That gives a `Default` value and a trivially cheap clone. The prepared configuration is the static `plain::PROFILE`, which is shared and not rebuilt.
- **Claims no extensions.** `extensions()` returns `$profile.extensions` from `plain::PROFILE`. The empty extension list is data in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/plain.rs#static[PROFILE]`. It is reached from the root by following the macro argument. The text only requires that no extensions are claimed. That is an observable result, so no separate structural clause applies.
- **Filename-based constructors select it.** The text says the constructors "select it when no supplied language claims the extension". This is observable behavior. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/contents.rs#impl[OutlineContent]/fn[parse_source]` shows the fallback. It tries `languages::registry().for_path(filename)`. If nothing matches, it calls `Self::parse_with(&languages::PlainText, ...)`. No other implementation is prescribed. A different fallback mechanism with the same selection results would still satisfy the text. The `{impl}` marker on `parse_source` is therefore not required, and it does no harm.

The cited requirements `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider` and `requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults` supply context only. The roots cover every structural obligation, so I found no gap.

behavioral: The tests cover each observable obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.plain-text.language`.

- **Claims no extensions.** `tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]` asserts `languages::PlainText.name() == "plain-text"` and `extensions().is_empty()`.
- **Selected when no language claims the extension, including no extension.**
  - `fn[unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors]` builds content for `missing.unclaimed`, `README` and `missing`. It asserts the plain-text outline: a file root plus one `line` child per nonblank line, with line selectors and spans.
  - `fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]` covers the other side of the fallback. It checks that each bundled language claims its own extensions, including upper-case ones such as `a.RS`. Those names are therefore not routed to plain text.
- **Implements `OutlineLang`.** The name and extensions assertions run through the trait. `outline_only_languages_report_unsupported_structural_search` also calls the trait's `search_structure` on `PlainText`. The outline operation is exercised through the plain-text outline tests.
- **Default value is cheaply cloneable.** I treated this as exempt. Clone sharing belongs to `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider`, and `PlainText` is a unit-like profile wrapper with no conditional or transformation to test. It is not a separate behavioral obligation here.
- **Filename-based constructors.** The fallback in `src/outline/contents.rs#impl[OutlineContent]/fn[parse_source]` is shared by those constructors. It consults the registry, then falls back to `PlainText`. Both branches are tested.

I found no behavioral obligation without a test, and no ambiguity in the text.

text: cheaply cloneable and claims no extensions. The filename-based constructors
select it when no supplied language claims the extension, including filenames
`OutlineLang` defines the language interface. Each implementation supplies its
name, claimed extensions, and outlining operation. Cloning a language shares
its prepared configuration instead of rebuilding it or copying it in proportion
to its size. Its result uses the public items, spans, and hashes under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.items`. Filename extensions omit the leading dot.
The filename-based constructors include Rust, Python, TypeScript, TSX,
Markdown, CSS, TOML, and YAML languages. Extension matching is
case-insensitive, using each implementation's claimed extensions.
A filename without a claimed extension uses the
[plain-text outline](sources/plain-text.md): a file root with one child per
